decision_conditions: The development to which this permission relates must be begun not later than the expiration of three years beginning with the date of the decision notice. Reason: To comply with the provisions of S.51 of the Planning & Compulsory Purchase Act 2004.

The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the following approved drawings and documents: SM-XX-S-DR-A-001,SM-XX-S-DR-A-002,SM-XX-00-3D-A-900,SM-XX-00-DR-A-101,SM-XX-00-DR-A-102,Location Plan,Design & Access Statement,Management Plan,Highway Safety Impact Form.Reason: For the avoidance of doubt and in the interests of proper planning.

The premises shall be used only as a children's care home for up to five children and for no other purpose, including any other purpose within Class C2 of the Schedule to the Town and Country Planning (Use Classes) Order 1987 (as amended), or in any provision equivalent to that Class in any statutory instrument revoking and re-enacting that Order, without the prior written permission of the Local Planning Authority. Reason: In the interests of residential amenity, car parking and highway safety, having regard to Policies DMD8 and DMD45 of the Enfield Development Management Document.

The development hereby permitted shall be occupied by no more than 5 residents and 3 members of staff (excluding ad hoc visiting specialists/ therapists) at any one time. Reason: In the interests of residential amenity, car parking and highway safety, having regard to Policies DMD8 and DMD45 of the Enfield Development Management Document.

Notwithstanding the details shown in the approved drawings and documents, the development hereby permitted shall not be occupied until details on a scheme of cycle parking have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Cycle parking shall be provided in accordance with minimum standards set out within the London Plan, with a requirement to provide a minimum of 1.no long stay cycle parking space, and 1.no short stay cycle parking space. Details shall be provided on proposed cycle stands, and a detailed floor plan drawing shall be provided detailing the configuration of the proposed cycle storage.The dedicated cycle store shall fulfil the following:-	Have aisles at least 1.5 metres wide to allow for easy manoeuvring.-	Provide a minimum width of at least 1 metre between stands.-	Provide step free access.-	Provide an access door with a minimum width of at least 1.2 metres.-	Be secured with a British Standard mortice lock or access fob to provide greater security.Approved cycle parking shall be provided on site prior to the first occupation of the development, and shall thereafter be retained unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Reason: To ensure that adequate cycle parking facilities are provided, and to promote sustainable modes of transport.

Notwithstanding the details shown on the submitted drawings, prior to the first occupation of the HMO hereby permitted, waste storage and recycling facilities to satisfy the permitted number of occupiers shall have been provided on site, in accordance with the Enfield's Household Recycling and Waste Planning Guidance for New Developments (February 2024). Such facilities are to be retained thereafter, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Reason: To ensure that adequate waste and recycling storage facilities are provided to meet the needs of future occupiers, promote sustainable waste management practices, and support borough-wide recycling targets.
description: Change of use of an existing dwellinghouse (Use Class C3) to a children's residential care home (Use Class C2) to accommodate up to five young persons, including internal reconfiguration only.
